body_es: AWS proporciona múltiples métodos y modelos para implementar y operar aplicaciones en la nube, cada uno con diferentes niveles de control y responsabilidad. IaaS (Infraestructura como Servicio) como Amazon EC2 ofrece máquinas virtuales completamente configurables que requieren gestión del sistema operativo. PaaS (Plataforma como Servicio) como AWS Elastic Beanstalk proporciona plataformas administradas para ejecutar aplicaciones sin gestionar infraestructura subyacente. SaaS (Software como Servicio) como Amazon Connect ofrece software completamente administrado listo para usar. Los contenedores con Amazon ECS y Amazon EKS permiten empacar y ejecutar aplicaciones de forma consistente. AWS Lambda habilita computación sin servidor donde el código se ejecuta en respuesta a eventos. Las herramientas de CI/CD como AWS CodePipeline automatizan completamente el despliegue. AWS CloudFormation permite infraestructura como código para reproducibilidad y versionado. La elección del modelo depende de requisitos de control, complejidad operativa y mantenibilidad. La eleccion correcta del modelo de implementacion depende de factores como: nivel de control requerido, experiencia operativa disponible, complejidad de mantenimiento, y presupuesto. EC2 (IaaS) ofrece maximo control pero requiere gestion integral del sistema operativo. Lambda (Serverless) minimiza responsabilidades operativas, cobrando solo por milisegundos ejecutados, ideal para cargas de trabajo impredecibles. ECS (Containers) proporciona balance entre control y automatizacion para aplicaciones microservicios. Elastic Beanstalk (PaaS) automatiza despliegue pero permite acceso a recursos subyacentes. Muchas organizaciones exitosas usan multiples modelos segun el requisito especifico de cada aplicacion. La hibridacion de modelos maximiza flexibilidad y eficiencia operativa.
body_en: AWS provides multiple methods and models for deploying and operating applications in the cloud, each with different control and responsibility levels. IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) such as Amazon EC2 offers fully customizable virtual machines requiring operating system management. PaaS (Platform as a Service) such as AWS Elastic Beanstalk provides managed platforms for running applications without managing underlying infrastructure. SaaS (Software as a Service) such as Amazon Connect offers fully managed ready-to-use software. Containers with Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS allow packaging and running applications consistently. AWS Lambda enables serverless computing where code runs in response to events. CI/CD tools like AWS CodePipeline completely automate deployment. AWS CloudFormation allows infrastructure as code for reproducibility and versioning. Choice of model depends on control requirements, operational complexity, and maintainability. Selecting the right deployment model depends on factors such as control level required, available operational expertise, maintenance complexity, and budget. EC2 (IaaS) offers maximum control but requires comprehensive operating system management. Lambda (Serverless) minimizes operational responsibilities, charging only for milliseconds executed, ideal for unpredictable workloads. ECS (Containers) provides balance between control and automation for microservices applications. Elastic Beanstalk (PaaS) automates deployment while allowing access to underlying resources. Many successful organizations use multiple models based on each application's specific requirements. Hybrid use of models maximizes operational flexibility and efficiency. Cloud-native applications typically combine multiple deployment models within a single architecture.
example_code:
# Launch an EC2 instance (IaaS)
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-12345678 --instance-type t3.micro --count 1

# Create an Elastic Beanstalk application (PaaS)
aws elasticbeanstalk create-application --application-name my-app

# Deploy Lambda function (Serverless)
aws lambda create-function --function-name my-function   --runtime python3.9 --role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lambda-role   --handler index.handler --zip-file fileb://function.zip

# Create CloudFormation stack
aws cloudformation create-stack --stack-name my-stack --template-body file://template.yaml
